How the energy industry works.

This is what you will be explaining to others.

1 · The problem

It is confusing on purpose.

In Sydney every home runs on the same network, the same wires. On top of it sit dozens of retailers and thousands of plans. Everyone already has power, so the game is to keep you from ever checking.

1
network, same wires to every home
30+
retailers reselling it
1,000s
of plans to hide behind

Confusopoly.

Keep it confusing enough and no one bothers to understand it.

So most people cannot read their own bill, they leave their plan untouched for years, and they pay far more than they need to.

This is how the energy companies make so much profit.

The two numbers they would rather you never learned.

Supply
Usage

Supply rate

A fixed cost you pay every day just to be connected, even if you use nothing. Like line rental.

Typically around $1.10 a day in NSW

Usage rate

What you pay for each unit of energy you actually use. The meter ticking.

Typically around 39c per kWh in NSW
Learn these two and every plan on the market suddenly makes sense. For a typical Sydney home the regulator's benchmark is about $1,965 a year on 3,900 kWh. Your two numbers put you above or below that.

Here's how your bill is really built.

Usage is nearly the whole thing, and it moves with how much you use. Supply barely changes. The difference between a good plan and a bad one hides in the rate you glance straight past.

Same street. Same wires. Wildly different bills.

Two homes next door can pay completely different rates for identical power. A few cents on the usage rate is hundreds a year. The only difference is who bothered to check.

That "$200 welcome credit" is bait. Here's how to make it yours.

They dangle a credit to sign you up, then lift the rate over the years they assume you'll stay. Take the offer, move on before the rate bites, and the bait becomes your profit.

The move: grab the welcome offer, ride the good rate, then compare again in about 6 months.

Keeping it honest

Three rules.

Energy comparison is a regulated market, so honesty is not a constraint, it is the brand.

1
You actually switch. Every story is real, from your own switch.
2
Only your own numbers. Talk about your bill and your saving, never a blended or invented figure.
3
Disclose the partnership. Paid content is marked as paid. Always.
